department: British Antarctic Survey (PhD in Antarctic Studies)

deadline.value: Funding deadline January 6, 2027 (apply by this date to enter the University funding competition); the final application deadline is later, but too late for most funding.

toefl_min.value: TOEFL iBT 100 overall with at least 25 in each section; this course sets its own English level.
toefl_min.quote: TOEFL Internet Score Element Score Listening 25 Writing 25 Reading 25 Speaking 25 Total 100

ielts_min.value: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall (Listening 7.0, Writing 7.0, Reading 6.5, Speaking 7.0).
ielts_min.quote: IELTS (Academic) Element Score Listening 7.0 Writing 7.0 Reading 6.5 Speaking 7.0 Total 7.0

supervisor.value: Research areas are advertised with a named supervisor; applicants name BAS supervisors in the application.
supervisor.quote: The research area will have a named supervisor and deadline for application clearly indicated.

funding.value: Most students are NERC CREATES-funded, but only a limited number of studentships exist.
funding.quote: DLAs offer a limited number of funded studentships.

entry_route.value: A high II.i honours degree (or international equivalent) is the stated standard; no master's is stated.
entry_route.quote: Applicants for this course should have achieved a High II.i Honours Degree.

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists for this field; ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

notes: In most cases applicants must be eligible for UKRI-NERC funding.
